label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Dear all,

Kiran, thank you for putting your concerns so plainly. Before answering them, I want to say clearly how thrilled I am that Amma and Appa are coming. Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays”, and Rohan is busy planning what Appa will grow. I don’t want the clumsy way I handled telling everyone to take away from any of that.

You are right that you should have been asked before the visa paperwork was under way. The idea itself came from Appa in August, when Rohan was showing him the vegetable patch on video and he said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” But once things started moving, I went into organising mode. I began the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, and that was exactly the point when I should have rung you. That’s on me, and I’m sorry.

On Appa’s heart, I agree that this needs a proper plan, not just reassurance. Dr. Prakash has agreed to do a full review in March before they fly, and a video consult with Appa in July. He knows the case and is happy to share his notes with me. I think the March review should be a firm checkpoint: if he has any concerns about the journey or the length of stay, we revisit the plan.

I also have a travel-insurance quote that specifically includes pre-existing cardiac cover. It is about £640 each for the six months, and the agent says it covers the stent. I’ll send you the full policy wording so we can look through the cover and exclusions properly rather than relying on a summary. I am not assuming that free NHS treatment will simply be available to them as visitors. Locally, Leicester Royal is 15 minutes from our house, and I know many of the cardiology team there, so I can help coordinate things quickly if ever needed.

Your point about Amma is fair too. Six months is a long time away from her house and her people, especially when she hasn’t stayed anywhere for more than six weeks since Paati died. The visa is the UK long-term visitor one, with a maximum of six months per visit; the proposed stay is from the first week of April to the end of September 2027. But there is no expectation that Amma must remain for the whole period just because that is the plan on paper. Her return ticket is flexible, and she can go home earlier whenever she wishes.

The annexe at the back is now finished, so they will have their own space rather than feeling parked in the middle of our household. It is ground floor, with no steps and its own shower with a grab rail.

Ganesh Chaturthi is something I should have discussed with you and Divya properly instead of simply presenting overlapping plans. Two possibilities occur to me. Amma and Appa could fly from Leicester to Pune in September for the festival and finish their trip there, rather than returning from here. Alternatively, you could all come to Leicester in August, and I would be very happy to cover the Pune family’s flights. Those are only suggestions for us to consider together, not another decision I am trying to make unilaterally.

Could we have a family video call this Sunday at 4pm UK time / 9.30pm India time? There is time before the visa submission in January, and I would much rather we talk through everyone’s concerns properly, and also hear directly from Appa and Amma about what would make the stay comfortable for them.

Lots of love,  
Meera
